If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% in late horizon (days 25–30) to avoid overestimation.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 2–5% in early horizon (days 1–10) to compensate for downward bias.  
If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 5 days, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in mid horizon (days 11–20) to reflect sentiment volatility.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 1–3% to forecast in late horizon to capture momentum.  
If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 1–3% from forecast in early horizon to avoid overcorrection.  
If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and forecast is above 70, reduce forecast by 5–10% in mid horizon to prevent overconfidence bias.
